models.purpose: Simulate one hour of a checkpoint as agents moving through four queues.
models.summary: Passengers are agents generated each second with probability gen-prob, then split 45 percent PreCheck. The checkpoint has four queues, q0 to q3, and ten processes with fixed times: document check 11.2 seconds, body scan 10.5, metal detector 1, pat-down 150, baggage search 200. A run generates for 3600 seconds and continues until the checkpoint empties. Configurations are four-digit codes; 1221 serves low traffic and 2243 high traffic.

variables.definition: probability a passenger arrives in a given second
four-digit count of officers and lanes
rate of passengers leaving the checkpoint

objectives: Simulate one hour of a checkpoint as agents moving through four queues.
constraints: at most one passenger arrives per second

parameter_estimation.method: generation probability 0.19 counted from the given sheet over nine minutes

steps: route each to the shortest lane
algorithm.convergence_criteria: run ends when the checkpoint is empty

identifiability_feasibility.analysis: five generation probabilities, two configurations, at least three runs each

strengths: every run is repeated at least three times and averaged
limitations: the prose says the figure reference is Figure 4 where the caption is Figure 1
missing_details: the number of trials beyond the stated minimum of three is not given

models.purpose: Locate the bottleneck by comparing mean wait across the four queues.
models.summary: Under configuration 1221 the mean total wait is 20.51 seconds at generation probability 0.09 and 232.39 at 0.18, with standard deviations 41.68 and 286.88. The longest queue is q3 except for regular passengers at 0.18, where it is q0. Under 2243 the standard deviation reaches 1409.13 seconds, about 23 minutes, at probability 0.72, while the summary sheet says it tops 30 minutes.

mean wait at the belt where belongings are collected

constraints: wait is time spent in queues only, not in processes
assumptions: a passenger joins the lane with the fewest people

models.purpose: Score each modification by the ratio of new throughput to old.
models.summary: Six modifications are scored as ratios. An extra metal detector raises throughput by factors 1.22 and 1.43 at probabilities 54 and 72. An extra body scanner, priced at about 250,000 dollars, cuts the standard deviation by more than a third at high traffic but lowers throughput by 7 percent at probability 9. Two PreCheck officers nearly double throughput over one; a third adds little. Raising PreCheck enrollment helps only up to 55 percent, then wait rises again.
